subject: dwarfBlacksmith
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf blacksmith at an anvil.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stout, ginger-bearded Warcraft-style dwarf smith in oversized riveted pauldrons and a leather apron, raising a sledge over a glowing half-forged blade held in tongs on an anvil and tree stump.
spec.layout: Chunky, hand-painted Blizzard proportions: the dwarf is about 1.4 m to the top of his head and nearly as broad as he is tall, with short sturdy legs, a barrel chest, a round belly, huge shoulders, big fists and a big head. He faces +Z and stands with his belly at z≈0.2. In front of him (z≈0.62) is a tree stump topped by a classic anvil, long axis along X, with the horn pointing to +X (the model's left). The anvil face is at y=0.78, so it sits at about waist height. His right hand (-X) holds a sledgehammer raised up and over the anvil. His left hand (+X) holds long tongs gripping a glowing, half-forged blade that lies on the anvil face. A few ember sparks float above the blade. Silhouette: two giant studded pauldrons, a horned helmet, a long braided ginger beard falling to the belt, a leather apron, and the glowing orange blade as the focal accent. The bottom of the stump and both boots rest on y=0. Style on every part: saturated, painterly colours, with each material built as a dark outline/shade base, a main colour and a small lighter highlight piece, e.g. a gold rim on every steel edge, rivets and studs in rows, chunky bevelled slabs rather than smooth forms, and exaggerated bold shapes. Warm light colours on top faces and cooler darker ones below. Everything that glows (blade, embers, sparks, forge-lit eyes' glints) uses the glow kit.

parts.builds: Everything from the hips down plus the waist. Two short, thick legs (thigh 0.25 m, shin 0.23 m, each a smooth sweep on the leg chain) in clothDark trousers, with leather knee guards (leatherLight plate, leatherDark strap, gold rivet) and calf wraps. Chunky boots in leather/leatherDark with a wide toe cap, a thick sole slab in iron, a steel toe cap with a gold rim, and fold-over cuffs at the top with three studs. Boots stand parallel with the toes pointing +Z. Around the pelvis: a broad belt (leatherDark with leatherLight edge sweep) with a big gold-rimmed buckle at the front showing a small steel anvil emblem, five studs on each side, and a short blue tabard skirt (cloth with a clothDark border and a gold trim stripe) front and back. Hanging from the belt: a small hammer loop, a leather pouch on the left hip, and a coil of rope on the right hip.
parts.attaches: The legs hang from hipL/hipR on joint hips; boots rest on y=0 (floor) at footL/footR. The belt sits on beltLine and the torso apron starts just above it.

parts.builds: Barrel chest and round belly as a loft on the spine: a clothDark undershirt, a thick leather apron (leather, leatherDark border sweep, stitched seam parts, soot smudges near the bottom, a gold rivet at each upper corner, a hammer-and-flame emblem patch in the centre built from small parts) hanging from a neck strap from chestCenter down to just above the belt, and a cross-chest strap. Two huge Warcraft-style pauldrons at shoulderL/shoulderR: layered steel plates (steelDark base, steel mid, steelLight edge highlights, gold rims), a row of rivets, and 3 chunky cone spikes on each, with a blue cloth shoulder cape piece under each. A steel gorget ring collar round the neck base. A short blue cloak panel hanging down the back with a gold edge. Sleeve openings are left for the arms: the arm part provides upper arms starting at the shoulder joints and the pauldrons cover their tops. Bare skin of the chest shows as a small V below the collar, hidden mostly by the beard.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, spine1 and spine2. Pauldrons are centred on shoulderL/shoulderR. The neck gorget meets the head part at neckBase. The belt of legsAndBelt starts at beltLine. Beard hangs in front of the apron's upper part, z>0.19.

parts.builds: The signature part: a big chunky head built on head/neck/jaw joints with a separate upper head and lower jaw (jaw hinge near the ear line). Wide skin skull with a strong brow ridge in skinShade, a large rounded bulbous nose (skinLight with a small shade underside), cheekbones, small pointed ears with gold hoop earrings, big eyes of eyeWhite with eyeBlue iris and ink pupil plus tiny white highlight, thick bushy ginger eyebrows (beard/beardLight blades) angled in a determined frown, ink eye outline. A walrus moustache of broad overlapping blades in beardDark root, beard mid and beardLight tip, swept out to the sides with gold rings. The huge beard: a solid wedge from chin to belt line plus about a dozen overlapping broad blades (root-to-tip beardDark, beard, beardLight), with two thick braids each with gold clasps and a beaded tip hanging down the chest front to y≈0.8. Helmet: a steel dome (steelDark under steel with a steelLight highlight rim) with a gold brow band, a nose guard strip, a row of rivets, two curved bone-coloured steel horns (steelLight with gold tips) rising out of the sides to a height of about 1.5 m, and ginger hair tufts sticking out below the helm at the back and sides, with a short braid at the back. Face stays clear: nothing in front of eyes and nose. The mouth is a dark ink gap between moustache and jaw with a few teeth.
parts.attaches: Head sits on neck at neckBase (neck sweep from spine2 into the head); head centre at headCenter, jaw on joint jaw. The beard root is at beardRoot and hangs over the torso apron without touching the belt. Helmet horns and hair stay inside the box.

parts.builds: Both arms, thick and muscular, in the rest pose given by the joints. Upper arms are skin sweeps emerging from the pauldrons (shoulderL/R to elbowL/R), forearms from elbow to wrist are heavy sweeps (about 0.07 m radius) covered with leatherDark bracers with steel plates, gold rivets and a lace strap. Big gauntleted fists: wide palm block in leather, finger blocks (4 fingers plus thumb) curled around the grips on fingersL/R and thumbL/R, with knuckle studs; the right fist wraps round the hammer handle at gripR (ring of fingers closed, hammer shaft passing through), the left fist round the tongs handles at gripL. Skin tones (skin, skinShade underside, skinLight top highlights) on the bare upper arm, with a few scars as small lighter strips and a gold armband on each bicep. Soot smudges (leatherDark flat patches) on the forearms. The hand parts stay slightly open on the sides so the tool handles can be seen between fingers.
parts.attaches: Starts at shoulderL/shoulderR (covered by the torso pauldrons), ends at the fists at gripL and gripR where the tools part's handles pass through the hands.

parts.builds: The handheld tools and the work in progress. (1) The sledgehammer, riding wristR: a wooden handle (wood, woodDark grip wrap with leather wraps) from gripR up and across toward hammerHead (rising about 0.2 m over the anvil and leaning toward +X), ending in a big chunky steel head block (steelDark base, steel body, steelLight face highlights, gold bands at both ends of the head) whose long axis is perpendicular to the shaft in the XY plane, so one striking face points down toward the blade; a pommel cap at the grip end with a gold ring. (2) The tongs, riding wristL: two long iron arms (iron with ironlike highlights in steelDark) crossing at a rivet pivot near the middle, handles running back past gripL to about z=0.24 with leather grip wraps, the jaws closing on the end of the blade at tongsJaw. (3) The half-forged blade lying along X on the anvil face centred on bladeCenter (about 0.38 m long, 0.07 wide, 0.02 thick, resting on y=0.78): a tapering extruded shape, glowing with a gradient of emberHot at the core, ember in the middle, emberDark at the cooler tip, plus a thin tang at the tongs end; use the glow kit on it. A few chips of glowing scale lie beside it. (4) 8–10 sparks, small glowing emberHot/ember cubes and tetrahedra of varied size flying from the hit zone up and out (around y 0.85–1.25 near x 0..0.3), all glowing. No paint on glowing parts.
parts.attaches: Hammer handle passes through the right fist at gripR (joint wristR); tongs handles through the left fist at gripL (joint wristL); the blade lies on anvilTop at bladeCenter and is gripped at tongsJaw.

parts.builds: The base the dwarf works on, static on joint base. A large tree-stump: wide low-poly cylinder (radius 0.33, wood with woodDark bark ring made of vertical ridges, leather-brown top cut face with concentric ring lines in woodDark, root flares at the bottom, a few small moss-free chips), top at stumpTop (y≈0.36). An iron band hoop (iron, gold rivet row) round the stump's upper rim. On it a classic big anvil, long axis along X: a wide base plate with foot blocks, a narrower waist, a thick steel face plate (steel with steelLight top edge, steelDark underside, iron wedge body) ending at y=0.78 (anvilTop) and about 0.58 m long × 0.2 m wide, a stepped heel at -X end with a round hardy hole and a pritchel hole in the top face, and a long tapering conical horn toward +X ending at x≈0.56 (the horn slightly lower than the face). A gold maker's mark and small scratch/dent parts on the side. Scorch marks (ink flat patches) and glow-tinted ember reflection strips on the face near the blade. At the base of the stump a bucket of water (wood staves, iron bands, a rope handle) and a few coal lumps (ink with ember glowing cracks) are NOT included; keep to a small pile of 3 coal lumps with ember glints at the stump's side near x=-0.35, z=0.85.
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor at floor mount; the anvil face top is anvilTop and the tools part's blade rests exactly there. The dwarf's boots stay clear of the stump's front edge (z<0.28).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out a rigged dwarf blacksmith character at an anvil in a Warcraft-inspired style, planning the dwarf's size and positioning facing the anvil, with a hammer, tongs, and a glowing forge element to complete the scene.

Now I'm working through the full skeleton hierarchy—hips, spine, chest, neck, head, arms, and legs—mapping out precise y-coordinates for each joint from feet to helmet, and positioning the shoulders and arms so one hand raises a hammer while the other holds tongs over the anvil.

Positioning the anvil itself atop a stump at waist height, figuring out the right y-level for its top surface and centering it in front of the dwarf for the forging pose.

Shoulder at z=0 for a forward hunch, with upper arm and forearm each around 0.28 so hands fall forward-down naturally.

Now I'm dividing the model into five parts: legs/boots covering the lower body with trousers, kilt, and belt tools within a bounding box roughly x[-0.3,0.3], y[0,0.75], z[-0.3,0.4]; torso covering chest, leather apron, pauldrons, and bandolier above that in y[0.7,1.15]; and I'm about to define the head section next.

Head includes face, braided beard, mustache, horned helmet or mohawk hair, ears and jaw, boxed in y[1.1,1.55]. I'm reconsidering the part split to six pieces: legs, torso, head, arms (with gauntlets and hands), tools (hammer, tongs, glowing workpiece, sparks — rigged to the wrist joints), and anvilStage (stump and anvil), budgeting roughly 130/170/190/150/110/110 triangles for a total under 900. Now I'm starting the joint hierarchy, beginning with the hips joint positioned at [0,0.6,-0.02] pointing upward.

Working through the spine chain from hips through spine1, spine2, neck, and head, adjusting positions and directions to get a natural upward-forward curve, then adding the jaw joint hinged near the ear. For the arms, I'm placing shoulderL on spine2 and computing the elbow and hand positions by projecting along a normalized rest-pose direction vector to get a down-forward-out arm pose.

Positioning the left hand gripping tongs resting on the anvil top, computing the wrist from the elbow using the chain length so the arm reaches naturally to that point, then setting up the shoulderL/elbowL/wristL chain with their own direction vectors, plus adding finger and thumb joints under the wrist with a digit role. Now starting on the right arm, which will be raised holding a hammer, beginning with the shoulderR position.

Still working out the hammer's grip and raised angle relative to the anvil...

I'll have the striking face point roughly downward toward the anvil, with the head perpendicular to the handle axis at its top end.

I'm settling on a rest pose where the shaft angles up and forward from the grip toward +x, with the head positioned so its striking face points down toward the workpiece, and I'll leave the exact cross-block orientation flexible for the builder to resolve against the strike direction.

Now I'm positioning the tongs in the left hand, running forward along +z from the wrist toward the workpiece on the anvil.

I'm recalculating the geometry so the anvil's z-range better matches the dwarf's reach, shifting the anvil center and checking the gap between belly and anvil front. I'm placing the hands around z=0.38 and working out the diagonal tong angle from hand to the workpiece's gripped end.

I'm positioning the tongs and hand grip coordinates, and defining the workpiece as a glowing bar along the x-axis being forged into a blade shape, with the hammer head positioned to strike near the cooler tip. I'm also verifying the hammer shaft vector from grip to head to make sure the swing geometry looks right.

Now I'm placing the anvil with its horn extending toward +x, adjusting the workpiece so it sits realistically on the anvil face and horn transition, and nudging the tongs jaws and hammer head position so the strike point lands correctly on the blade.

Checking the stump radius against the dwarf's boot position so the base doesn't clip the feet, then working out the overall bounding box — depth from the back at z=-0.32 to the stump front at z=0.95 gives about 1.3 total length, and I'm now checking the width from the pauldrons outward.

Now I'm sketching the dwarf's proportions following a Warcraft-style aesthetic: broad shoulders, oversized hands, a wide chest, and a big head topped with a horned helmet, with a braided beard that hangs down toward the belt and needs its own bounding box that may overlap the torso.

I'm defining the color palette next — saturated, chunky Warcraft tones for skin, ginger-red Ironforge-style beard braids, dark hair, and steel armor accents.

Adding a few more tones and capping the palette at 24 colors, then laying out the leg joint hierarchy with short dwarf proportions for thigh, shin, and ankle, plus considering whether to add beard braid joints as a separate chain.

Thinking through parts without their own joints, like the anvil or helmet — deciding whether they should attach to the nearest existing joint (hips) or whether I need a dedicated static root joint so they don't move unintentionally with the rig.

Now I'm working through the mount point coordinates for the anvil top, the blade, the tongs jaw, and hand grips, placing each precisely relative to the anvil's position.

I'm continuing to lay out the remaining body mounts—neck, head, beard, belt, shoulders, hammer—then starting to define the bounding boxes for the leg and torso geometry, including the boots and pauldron extents.

Next, I'm defining boxes for the head, arms with bracers and gauntlets, and the tools section covering the hammer, tongs, blade, and sparks, followed by the anvil stage dimensions.

Settling the leg box dimensions and planning the Warcraft-style description details: oversized spiky pauldrons, hand-painted shading with highlight/dark layering, and glow accents for embers, blade, and sparks. I'm allocating a budget across parts—legs 130, torso 190, head 190, arms 120, tools 120, anvil 110—and now writing out the full joint list and layout as valid JSON.

Mapping out the skeleton hierarchy: base, hips, spine1/spine2, neck, head, jaw, then the leg chain (hip, knee, ankle, toe) with roles and directions assigned, mirroring the right side with negated x values.

Now I'm continuing to the arms, placing shoulder, elbow, wrist joints off the spine with calculated direction vectors, then adding finger and thumb joints branching off the wrist.

Working out fingers and thumb placement so the hammer shaft passes naturally through the fist, then moving on to write out the final spec with sizing details.
